content.jointProblem: Can a site-specific, unsupervised anomaly detector be built and calibrated on ArmaturaSec's unlabelled Modbus and BACnet traffic archives, and produce alerts accurate enough and explainable enough for plant operators while running on ProtoSense/on-device hardware? The work would test whether Kiss's statistical and one-class baseline methods transfer from Modbus/DNP3 evidence to BACnet and to ArmaturaSec's real deployments.

rationale.text: Kiss has directly built per-register statistical baselines and a one-class Modbus/TCP detector on a live substation testbed, matching ProtoSense's need to learn site-specific normal behaviour.

sources.quote: per-register statistical baselines for Modbus/TCP traffic captured over six months on a live substation automation testbed

rationale.text: Her work includes post-hoc threshold calibration using unlabelled operational data, which targets the false-alarm problem ArmaturaSec describes.

sources.quote: post-hoc calibration procedure using a small set of unlabelled operational data

rationale.text: She has developed incremental Gaussian-mixture online detection for ICS traffic without periodic full retraining, relevant to baseline drift on long-running client sites.

sources.quote: incremental variant of Gaussian mixture modelling (iGMM) for online anomaly detection in ICS traffic

rationale.text: She is open to joint projects and contract research on ICS anomaly detection deployment, so the collaboration format fits her stated interests.

sources.quote: joint projects with companies deploying ICS monitoring solutions
contract research on protocol traffic analysis and anomaly detection deployment

rationale.text: She has practical validation experience with an energy distributor and water utility and has consulted on SCADA anomaly-detection requirements.

sources.quote: providing practical validation of research methods on operational infrastructure
paid consulting for a mid-size automation integrator on specifying anomaly detection requirements for a SCADA upgrade project

rationale.text: Her group operates an ICS testbed with Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators and long-term packet capture infrastructure.

sources.quote: dedicated ICS testbed equipped with Siemens-compatible PLCs, Modbus/TCP and DNP3 traffic generators, and packet capture infrastructure

constraints.text: The method must work without labelled attack examples and learn a site-specific normal baseline; evaluation cannot rely on supervised attack labels.

sources.quote: we have nothing labelled as malicious
What we actually need is something that learns what normal looks like on a specific site and raises a flag when behaviour drifts from that baseline.

constraints.text: Alert thresholds must be calibrated to avoid the false-positive overload that already caused clients to disable alerts.

sources.quote: flagged so many false positives in real deployments that clients started switching the alerts off
post-hoc calibration procedure using a small set of unlabelled operational data

constraints.text: Outputs must be explainable to a plant manager in plain language.

sources.quote: We need a method that works with no attack examples and that we can explain to a plant manager in plain language.

constraints.text: Inference must run on-device within the packet-forwarding latency budget, potentially on the planned security processor.

sources.quote: dedicated security processor to support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency

constraints.text: Work depends on NDA access to traffic archives, hardware bench, and firmware codebase.

sources.quote: access to our traffic archives, our hardware bench, and our existing firmware codebase under NDA

constraints.text: Kiss's testbed access is under a data-sharing agreement.

sources.quote: Her group's testbed capacity is available to industrial partners under a data-sharing agreement.

risks: BACnet/IP is not covered by the cited publications; transfer from Modbus/DNP3 and mixed-protocol evidence to BACnet must be tested before any performance claim.
ArmaturaSec has no confirmed malicious captures, so detection performance can only be estimated through controlled injection or red-team exercises, not real attack labels.
The explainability requirement is not directly evidenced in Kiss's publications; a plain-language alert rationale may need joint design and operator testing.
False-positive calibration may still fail on client sites with twenty years of unmonitored traffic and unusual but legitimate behaviour.
Kiss's availability is unknown, and the company can dedicate only one to two engineers part-time; scheduling and any PhD supervision capacity need confirmation.
NDA and data-sharing terms may limit publication, dataset release and reuse of the firmware codebase; the 2021 student project was not continued formally.
On-device deployment may depend on the planned fifth hardware variant and dedicated security processor, which is a late-2025 plan, not current evidence.
questions: Which archives contain BACnet/IP versus Modbus TCP, how many sites and years do they span, and what metadata or consent restrictions apply?
Can ArmaturaSec provide controlled attack injection or red-team scenarios on a bench or consenting pilot site to evaluate detectors without real labels?
What are the target hardware, memory, CPU and latency budgets for ProtoSense inference, and will the fifth variant be available for the project?
What alert explanation must a plant manager see, in which language, and what false-alarm rate per site per day is acceptable?
Does Kiss have capacity to supervise an industrial PhD candidate, or should this be a joint project or contract research, and under what data-sharing agreement?
Which company engineers will be assigned, and can they work with Kiss's group under the NDA on firmware integration?
How will success be measured: AUROC or AUPRC on injected scenarios, alert precision at a fixed false-alarm budget, or operator acceptance?
